notes: TBox rule edit: karst, formed by water dissolving soluble rock, is said to form in volcanic rock. Derivability very_unlikely: the definition is stated directly. No real exceptions: landforms in volcanic rock that look like karst are called pseudokarst, not karst; the original names 'soluble rock' (limestone, dolomite, gypsum) and the answers say limestone, which is right for every member asked. New members: Gunung Sewu and the Causse Méjean (limestone per Wikipedia). The two background queries ask well-known members whose property a model likely also stores by name (README, TBox). For each member, one world keeps the stored property and the member stops counting as a member of the class; the other keeps the membership and applies the edited rule. The two members' choices are independent, so the worlds combine them (four). Lopsided worlds are kept (README Decisions 4). New members changed in verification: the Tsingy de Bemaraha and the Stone Forest are famous limestone sites ('Tsingy AND limestone' 11,546, 'Stone Forest AND limestone' 11,781, approximate), so their rock may be stored by name. Gunung Sewu (1,727 Dolma mentions; Wikipedia: 'the karst region of southern central Java') and the Causse Méjean (1,020; Wikipedia: 'a limestone plateau') are rarely described by their rock ('AND limestone' 72 and 31, approximate). Java's volcanoes are a lure toward the new answer, not a competing stored fact about Gunung Sewu's rock. The either-or questions take one value for granted; since 2026-10-31 this is stated as a bridge of the two well-known-member queries ('A landscape formed in limestone is not formed in volcanic rock.'), which is why each world gives up either the membership or the stored value (formal check, FINDINGS B3/C3).
